| Maximum capacity (Emax) | 25 t | 30 t up to and including 50 t |

This is interesting. The table has two columns for Maximum capacity: "25 t" and "30 t up to and including 50 t". This suggests the cert covers two variants:
1. Emax = 25 t
2. Emax from 30 t to 50 t (range)

And Rated Output varies: 1.6 mV/V for the 25t model, 2.0 mV/V for the 30-50t models.

Hmm, this is a bit ambiguous. The first column pair (25 t, 1,6 mV/V) and second column (30 t up to and including 50 t, 2,0 mV/V). So there are two model variants by Emax:

Model 1: Emax = 25 t, Rated output = 1.6 mV/V
Model 2: Emax = 30–50 t, Rated output = 2.0 mV/V

Other characteristics are common (span both columns with colspan=2): Minimum dead load 0 kg, Accuracy class C, n = 5500, Y = 19000, Z = 5500, input impedance, temp range, pLC = 0.7, humidity class CH, safe overload 150% of Emax, output impedance, excitation, material, atmospheric protection.

So I should model this as a model_family with two models:
- model_id: "Emax=25t"
- model_id: "Emax=30-50t"

And model_level characteristics:
- maximum_capacity: 25 t for model 1, {min:30, max:50} t for model 2

The schema doesn't have a tolerance field per se, but characteristics values are objects with value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. Maybe add extra keys? The schema is strict: "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape" — value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers. I shouldn't add extra fields. So {min:1100, max:1220}, unit "Ω".

Actually wait — maybe I could split into two: input_impedance_nominal (1160) and input_impedance_tolerance (±60)? That's over-engineering. I'll use min/max.
